_comment: D-14: the one runbook_progress key both languages agree on by name, not only by convention. Every other key in app/src/state/phases.ts is read by the app alone -- Python never checks whether a volunteer ticked 'Forum announcement seeded'. RETRIEVED_TICK (tools/convener_ops/journey/platform_fcc.py) is the sole exception: release_recording's own gate reads runbook_progress[RETRIEVED_TICK] before it will let a recording be deleted, and phases.ts's own journey is where a host actually ticks it. If the two ever spelled this differently, the tick a host sees and ticks in the app would silently stop being the one the CI job checks -- a recording could then be deleted with no real evidence behind the box that was supposed to prove it, or, the safer failure, never deletable at all because the app's tick can never satisfy a check reading a different key. Pinned from both sides: tools/tests/journey/test_platform_fcc.py asserts RETRIEVED_TICK equals this value; app/tests/state/phases.test.ts asserts the same key appears, once, in app/src/state/phases.ts's own delivered-phase items.
